newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Sydney Olympics attract A$500 mln sponsorship.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Sydney Olympics attract A$500 mln sponsorship.

text.p: The organisers of the Sydney 2000 Olympics on Tuesday announced a list of 17 international and Australian firms who will provide sponsorship worth more than A$500 million in cash and services.
The list of "Team Millennium Partners" was headed by nine traditional worldwide Olympic sponsors such as The Coca-Cola Co, International Business Machines Corp and Eastman Kodak Co.
They were joined by eight "national partners" including Australian resources group The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and Westpac Banking Corp.
Other Australian companies on the list were state telecoms carrier Telstra Corp, property group Westfield Trust, the Australia Mutual Provident Society (AMP), airline Ansett energyAustralia.
Swiss watchmaker SMH is also a national partner through its popular Swatch brand, Sydney organisers said.
The 17 companies will have the right to associate themselves with the Sydney Games for a four-year period beginning on Wednesday.

Sydney organising committee chief executive Mal Hemmerling told a news conference that the committee was hoping to sign up extra partners in the coming months but the total number of sponsors, at around 22, would still be only half the number signed up for the 1996 Atlanta Games.

Hemmerling and Sydney Olympic marketing manager John Moore declined to say what each company would be paying for the sponsorship deal, but said the minimum floor set by the organising committee was around A$25 million.
The nine worldwide or TOP sponsors have deals negotiated directly with the International Olympic Committee, with Sydney receiving a portion of the revenue.

Moore said the organising committee expected to receive around A$180 from worldwide TOP sponsors out of a total sponsorship target of up to A$700 million. Of a total budget of A$2.4 billion, about A$1.2 billion is being met by the sale of television rights.
Other worldwide sponsors were credit card company Visa International, United Parcel Service of America Inc, McDonald's Corp, Panasonic, Time and Fuji Xerox.
